Incorporating the August 2021 Beige Book, the outlook remains positive but more mixed than the SLOOS-alone read. District reports pointed to moderate growth, broad-based labor shortages, and accelerating wage gains, with price increases widespread due to supply-chain and input-cost pressures. Delta-related headwinds slowed activity in leisure and hospitality and constrained production in some industries. At the same time, demand remained solid, and credit availability and loan demand were generally supportive—consistent with the FOMC’s view that financial conditions are accommodative and with its “taper soon” signal. Net effect: the Beige Book tempers the upside from SLOOS by highlighting capacity constraints and cost pressures, but does not undercut a self-sustaining recovery.
